name: argus
description: Runtime evidence from a live Windows process: memory, disassembly, IAT resolution, call-chain tracing, and a hypothesis ledger.
long_description:
Other reverse-engineering MCP servers bridge a static analyzer and hand the agent the file on disk. Argus attaches to a running Windows process and returns what the program actually became: real bytes at real addresses, disassembly of the code that executed, resolved IAT thunks, caller chains walked from live memory, and recovered structures.

A processor cannot execute ciphertext, so packing, string encryption and runtime-resolved imports all have to be undone before the code runs. At that instant the truth is sitting in memory in the clear.

Built for recovering protocols from software whose servers no longer exist, where the client binary is the only surviving specification. Also useful for malware analysis, interoperability work, and debugging memory corruption.

argus-router inspects the target, decides whether it is x86 or x64, and dispatches to the matching engine, so one configured binary handles both native x64 and WOW64 targets.

tools.name: processes_list
tools.description: List running Windows processes so the AI can find a target PID before reading runtime memory.

tools.name: processes_find
tools.description: Find running process candidates by name substring, exact image name, or PID.

tools.name: runtime_imports
tools.description: Parse PE32 import/IAT data from the live mapped process image.

tools.name: runtime_exports
tools.description: Parse PE export tables from live mapped modules and return exported API names with runtime VA/RVA evidence.

tools.name: resolve_api_targets
tools.description: Resolve runtime API targets from loaded module exports.

tools.name: resolve_iat_thunks
tools.description: Find x86 import thunks such as jmp/call dword ptr [IAT] and return the runtime target plus thunk address.

tools.name: disasm_at
tools.description: Decode 32-bit runtime instructions at an address using a targeted memory window.

tools.name: analyze_function
tools.description: Disassemble one runtime function body from a targeted memory window until ret/count and collect direct callees.

tools.name: scan_x86_call_sites
tools.description: Find direct x86 E8/E9 call/jump sites to a target, annotate each with instruction text and best-effort function start.

tools.name: analyze_send_call_sites
tools.description: For a send/thunk target, scan executable call sites and return compact evidence from preceding instructions: push immediate opcode candidates, push string addresses, and packet-shaped C_/S_ names.

tools.name: extract_dispatch_tables
tools.description: For a recv dispatcher, identify index/jump table candidates from runtime instructions and, when tables are found or provided, output opcode -> dispatch index -> stub -> handler evidence with opcode_value_location.

tools.name: trace_call_chain
tools.description: Walk callers upward from a runtime target for a bounded number of depths.

tools.name: mem_read
tools.description: Read runtime memory at an address and return AI-first evidence with module/RVA, region flags, byte context, ASCII preview, and next-tool hints.

tools.name: mem_write
tools.description: Write exact bytes to runtime memory and return the write evidence.

tools.name: mem_read_chain
tools.description: Read a pointer chain using original Argus semantics: dereference base, add offsets, dereference intermediate nodes, then return final bytes.

tools.name: read_struct
tools.description: Read consecutive 4-byte words and report raw u32 values plus possible pointer target region evidence.

tools.name: correlate_addr
tools.description: Convert between live process address, RVA, and Ghidra/static address using the main module base.

tools.name: locate
tools.description: Evidence chain matching original Argus: scan string, find pointers to it, keep executable refs, and return best-effort containing function starts.

tools.name: find_vtable
tools.description: Find x86 MSVC RTTI/vtable evidence: TypeDescriptor string, COL, vtable address, and method slots.

tools.name: diff_struct
tools.description: Overlay static struct fields from Hydra /structs/{name} or provided fields onto live memory and return raw field bytes plus pointer-region evidence.

tools.name: record_hypothesis
tools.description: Append an unverified AI hypothesis to the evidence ledger.

tools.name: add_evidence
tools.description: Attach external/static/dynamic evidence to an existing hypothesis record.

tools.name: verify_hypothesis
tools.description: Mark a hypothesis as verified or contradicted.

tools.name: query_hypotheses
tools.description: Read the evidence ledger by entity/status/claim_type and include negative knowledge for an entity.

tools.name: real_rate
tools.description: Return verified/total and counts by status/source/claim type from the evidence ledger.

tools.name: mem_attach
tools.description: Compatibility alias for original Argus mem_attach.

tools.name: mem_modules
tools.description: List target process modules with base addresses and image sizes for RVA correlation.

tools.name: memory_regions
tools.description: List committed runtime memory regions with base, size, kind, and protection flags so AI can distinguish image/private/executable/readable areas before scanning.

tools.name: scan_string
tools.description: Scan readable runtime memory for an exact string.

tools.name: scan_regex
tools.description: Scan readable runtime memory with a regex, for packet names such as C_[A-Za-z0-9_]+ or S_[A-Za-z0-9_]+.

tools.name: scan_bytes
tools.description: Scan runtime memory for an AOB pattern.

tools.name: scan_pointers_to
tools.description: Scan readable runtime memory for pointers to an address and return AI-first pointer evidence.

tools.name: scan_callers
tools.description: Scan executable readable regions for x86 E8/E9 rel32 callers or jumpers to a target address.

tools.name: value_scan_start
tools.description: Start a typed value investigation scan.

tools.name: value_scan_refine
tools.description: Refine value candidates using a fresh memory read.

tools.name: value_explain
tools.description: Explain one value candidate as AI-first evidence with local bytes, region/module context, typed numeric value, and next-tool hints.
